articles.title: This GTA 6 Glitch (Almost) Ruined The Game’s Most Iconic Scene
articles.summary: Note: This story will discuss a pivotal mission in Chapter 2 of Grand Theft Auto 6. A powerful sequence in Grand Theft Auto 6 is quickly becoming a favorite among the game's many players, but a technical mishap made my experience of this scene very different--hilariously different.
body: Chapter 2 of GTA 6 begins with Jason and Lucia in a rough spot, with the former still recovering from major injuries sustained at the end of Chapter 1, and the latter having to care for him. It isn't until the mission "Breakfast Run" that Jason is back on his feet, and the Bonnie-and-Clyde-like duo mark his recovery with a crime spree.

Set to "Money or Nothing" by Dire Straits, Lucia and Jason rob a diner, not dissimilar to a scene from Pulp Fiction, and a playable montage shows the pair robbing convenience shops, a clothing store, and other establishments. The image of Jason and Lucia busting open double doors, guns in hand, is probably the most iconic image of GTA 6, a statement of intent that defines the game's story going forward.

But somehow, I had gotten a slightly different version of this montage. When I returned to the motel as Lucia, I sprinted toward the door, only for the game to place me back outside the room. The game told me to "Go to Hank's Waffles" with no additional context, and I walked back into the motel to find Jason, not only up and about, but only sporting his underwear, bandages, and a buzz cut.

articles.title: GTA 6 Was Biggest Launch in PlayStation History
articles.summary: Now that the dust has somewhat settled after the avalanche that was the launch of GTA 6, PlayStation has revealed some of its stats from the game, revealing that this was the single largest game release in PlayStation history.
body: PlayStation’s November 23 blog post states that more than 39 million unique players have played the game on the PlayStation 5, setting a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any PlayStation game. This beats out other records for multiplayer games, single-player games, and perhaps most astonishingly, even free-to-play titles.

On top of that, GTA 6 players logged a total of 683 million hours played in the game, with the average player spending an estimated 17.4 hours sticking up virtual pawn shops and stealing NPC’s cars during its first few days.

What’s more impressive is the sheer amount of people who purchased PS5s specifically to play GTA 6. PlayStation’s blog says it saw the “largest number of newly-connected PS5 consoles on a single day” since the console’s launch in November 2020, not counting end-of-year holidays like Christmas. Since GTA 6’s launch, it was the first game played on 70% of these new consoles.

GTA 6 has, perhaps unsurprisingly, broken a slew of big records. The most prominent of these is its status as the biggest entertainment launch of all time, with Rockstar reporting that the game earned $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours.

articles.title: GTA 6's Best Easter Egg Is a Classic Tom Cruise Crime-Thriller You Can Stream For Free
articles.summary: One of Grand Theft Auto 6 ’s strangest random encounters occurs when you’re offering taxi services, and a man with a beard wearing a dark suit and sunglasses climbs into the backseat with a gun.
body: Jason or Lucia gets a better deal than Mann’s cabbie in this Easter egg. If you take the stranger to his destination and follow him inside after he takes out some of the criminals there, you can find a ton of valuable loot. Most players seem keen on eliminating the stranger rather than keep driving him around. In Collateral, Jamie Foxx’s character, Max, has to spend the whole night driving Cruise’s Vincent around Los Angeles. If you’ve never seen how that goes for him, Collateral is streaming for free on Pluto TV — and it’s a must-watch, especially if you want a movie that has a vibe as wild and crime-filled as GTA 6 ’s.

Max is a cab driver who’s been telling himself for years that the job is temporary. He wants to start his own limo company someday, so when a well-dressed passenger named Vincent (Cruise) offers him $600 to drive him around for the night, it seems like the kind of opportunity that could get him a little closer to quitting. Then a body lands on his cab at their first destination. Vincent has five people to kill before the night is over. Max has just agreed to drive him to all five stops — and he’s already an accomplice.

articles.title: GTA 6’s Donnie Actor Underwent Brain Surgery While He Was Awake And Playing Guitar
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 features a big cast of characters with fascinating, memorable storylines, and one such character is the drug-smuggler Donnie. He's played by actor Brad Carter, and he has a captivating life story of his own.
body: Some 13 years ago, Carter underwent brain surgery to address tremors in his hands. For his brain surgery, he needed to be awake for the best chance at success, and as a musician, he played guitar to help the surgeon place the electrodes in the right positions.

His surgery was documented live on Twitter and Vine back in 2013, and you can see some dramatic photos of the surgery on UCLA's website. The surgery, or actually the multiple surgeries he had, did not completely eliminate his tremors, but he was able to play guitar again. The story made international headlines.

Carter's role as Donnie may be the part he ends up being known best for, considering how enormous and culturally dominating GTA 6 is. But he had a long acting and music career before GTA 6, having appeared on episodes of It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia, Dexter, True Blood, True Detective, Justified, Ozark, Yellowstone, and Sons of Anarchy.
GTA 6 is Carter's second big gaming role, following his portrayal of Jonah in Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption (2010).

body: It’s October 2001, and you’re standing in a dimly lit game store, where rows upon rows of boxes sit in anticipation as you glance across their titles, unsure exactly which among them you'll end up taking home. Unfortunately, you can only pick one. Your eyes are already darting between Devil May Cry, Silent Hill 2, and Ico, which all feel eerily attuned to those pre-Halloween vibes. Noticing your indecisiveness (and the look of impatience on your mother’s face), the store clerk strides over with an assist, placing in your hands a game you had never heard of until that very moment.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

articles.title: GTA 6 Is So Unstoppable It's Even Made Nickelback Go Viral
articles.summary: It's still a debate whether Grand Theft Auto 6 has the best gaming soundtrack of 2026, but it certainly has the most soundtrack of 2026. Rockstar Games' latest open-world crime epic features more than 800 songs, most of which you'll hear on its 26 genre-themed radio stations.
body: You might be somewhat surprised to hear "How You Remind Me" making the rounds again, years removed from its days reigning over the Billboard charts. To this day, the most-played radio song of the 2000s has been relegated to background music in the daddest bars from Mississauga to Massapequa. It is arguably the epitome not just of Dad Rock but specifically of Divorced Dad Rock. If "How You Remind Me" was a person, its kitchen would include Slim Jims (assorted flavors), cold pizza (definitely pepperoni), and nothing else. It would drive a 2014 Corvette Stingray (bright red, obviously). It would live on the golf course.

But with "Ola Afta Poui Fovamai," Protopsalti injects a youthful, upbeat verve to Chad Kroeger's genius composition that legendarily emerged, nearly fully formed, from his brain in just 45 minutes following an argument with a partner. It's the sort of track you'd play in a convertible on a sunny day, or in the bathroom while getting ready for a party themed after The Devil Wears Prada (the good one). There is practically zero Divorced Dad energy in "Ola Afta Poui Fovamai." It is transformational.
points: It's still a debate whether Grand Theft Auto 6 has the best gaming soundtrack of 2026, but it certainly has the most soundtrack of 2026.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6’s HDR Is Broken, But These Tweaks Can Fix It
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI is a visual and audial treat, and is easily one of the most technically impressive games on the current generation of consoles. But it isn't without issues, especially if you're trying to experience the sights and sounds of Vice City with all the moody contrast and bright…
body: That's due to an HDR calibration tool that isn't exactly working in the way that you expect it. Like many other games, GTA VI doesn't use the system-level HDR settings on either the PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X|S. Instead it features its own calibration tool, which lets you adjust the maximum brightness, black levels, and paper white values that work best on your display. While the tool makes calibration seem straightforward, there's an issue with it that makes it very unreliable.

Specifically, the maximum brightness and paper white point values seem to be linked in a way that is both unclear and incorrect. Normally you would set these values individually, with maximum brightness set according to the value your display supports and the paper white value that looks best to you. GTA VI instead changes the maximum peak brightness value it is storing as you change the paper white point. For example, if you set a maximum peak brightness at 1000 nits (a typical value) but then reduce the paper white point (given how how its default is), the peak brightness value reduces as well, with no indication to you that it's happening.
points: Grand Theft Auto VI is a visual and audial treat, and is easily one of the most technically impressive games on the current generation of consoles.

articles.title: The 6 Most Outrageous GTA 6 Myths, Debunked
articles.summary: After a wild opening weekend, Grand Theft Auto 6 is off to the races. Millions are playing Rockstar’s enormous open-world game and discovering its complexities in real time.
body: Because of that, there are a lot of myths about GTA 6 currently floating around the internet. Some come from harmless misunderstandings, while others are more deliberate misrepresentations intended to scare off potential players. To help you navigate the noise, we’ve rounded up some of the most rampant myths currently circulating around GTA 6 and fact-checked them accordingly.
The claim: GTA 6 ’s story forces you to do chores for Lucia instead of crimes.
The claim: GTA 6 doesn’t allow you to steal cars, or heavily restricts what you can steal.

While there’s a grain of truth to this, it has been heavily exaggerated on social media. There are some select cars that you can’t steal in GTA 6, like those around Jason’s neighborhood or in an NPC’s car lot. But for the most part, you can jack just about any vehicle you see in Leonida. The catch is that you’ll need a device that can copy keys to get into some of the more expensive cars, and you won’t get that until Chapter 3. Being able to steal anything requires some patience as you play through the story, but be rest assured that you can do as much grand theft auto as ever in Grand Theft Auto.
points: After a wild opening weekend, Grand Theft Auto 6 is off to the races.

articles.title: Trump claims credit for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, posts meme depicting Huang holding up a bra victoriously
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he personally "convinced" the Nvidia board to reinstate Jensen Huang. Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO a little under two weeks ago after admitting to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang (no relation), who formerly controlled Singaporean tech…
body: Following the admission, as well as reports of two other affairs with Nvidia employees, Huang resigned as Nvidia president, CEO, and board member. Last week, amid calls for Huang's return from tech CEOs and investors, the Nvidia board said firmly that it would not reinstate him.

Cue the It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia title card: The gang reinstated him. On Monday, the Nvidia board said that it had "voted unanimously" to bring Huang back after receiving "input from senior levels of the United States government." Nvidia shares shot up 31.48% during Monday's trading.

Trump has taken credit for the change of heart. "I made the deal," he told CNBC. The President also posted a congratulatory AI-generated image depicting Huang as himself surviving an attempted assassination while holding up a red bra victoriously.
The news of Huang's reinstatement prompted a flurry of responses from US congressmembers on Monday.

articles.title: Deltarune Chapter 6 is playable "from the beginning to the end," Toby Fox says, but the RPG's final part has "only just started"
articles.summary: Toby Fox has given eager fans an update on the development of Deltarune Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 - the Undertale follow-up's final two episodes.
body: While the bones are supposedly all there, Fox explained that he and his team still need to knock out localisation, testing and polishing. "Much of the game looks complete… but, some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing."

Deltarune Chapter 6 was previously described as a slightly shorter episode that should hopefully set up the game's finale quite nicely. Despite being on the smaller side, Fox said he understandably doesn't want to rush development and "would like it to be as good as possible."
And since Deltarune's next chapter is almost past the finish line - at least, in some respect - that means certain members of the team have already moved over to Chapter 7.
"Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence."

articles.title: Sony: GTA 6 set record for 'highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation' ever
articles.summary: GTA 6 has been shattering records since before it came out, becoming the top-rated game in the history of Metacritic before it had the biggest entertainment launch (by dollars) in history. Sony is now joining in that victory lap by sharing GTA 6 milestones as they pertain to PlayStation.
body: "More than 39 million unique players have experienced Jason and Lucia's story in Grand Theft Auto 6 on PlayStation 5," Sony content communications manager Tim Turi wrote in a blog post today. That is a staggering number, especially considering GTA 6 also launched on Xbox and will (eventually) hit PC.

But that's not a sales record—Rockstar still has a ways to go to surpass GTA 5's 230 million lifetime sales. What is unprecedented, at least for PlayStation, is GTA 6's concurrents over launch weekend.
"GTA 6 set a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer, free-to-play, and single-player titles," Turi said.

That's the wild one to me, because that means more people were playing GTA 6 at the same time on the largest console platform than Call of Duty, GTA 5, or even Fortnite has ever achieved. Turi didn't share the concurrent figure itself, which is too bad—Steam remains the only platform that hands out exact player data. If the figure is theoretically higher than some of the biggest concurrent peaks we know about on Steam, then it could've been as high as 3-4 million players.
points: GTA 6 has been shattering records since before it came out, becoming the top-rated game in the history of Metacritic before it had the biggest entertainment launch (by dollars) in history.
